title: Why Findings Must Be Replicated
text:
Researchers often rely on controlled experiments to establish causal relationships. In a well-designed study, participants are randomly assigned to groups, which reduces the influence of hidden variables. However, a single experiment rarely provides conclusive evidence, because its results may depend on particular conditions.

For this reason, scientists prefer to replicate findings across different laboratories and populations. When multiple independent teams obtain similar results, confidence in the original claim grows considerably. Conversely, failures to replicate prompt a careful reexamination of the methods used.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why is random assignment used in a well-designed study?
options: To reduce the influence of hidden variables
To eliminate the need for control groups

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what increases confidence in an original claim?
options: Similar results from multiple independent teams

questions.text: What can be inferred about the results of a single experiment?
options: They may not hold under different conditions
They are always more reliable than replications
They prove a causal relationship completely

questions.text: What does the writer imply about failed attempts to replicate a finding?
options: They can lead scientists to re-examine their methods
They prove the original finding was fraudulent
They should be ignored by researchers
They are usually caused by a lack of funding

vocabulary.definition: proving something beyond any reasonable doubt
showing that one thing directly produces another
factors that can change or affect the outcome of a study
to repeat a study to check whether its results are the same

paragraph_translations: Los investigadores suelen recurrir a experimentos controlados para establecer relaciones causales. En un estudio bien diseñado, los participantes se asignan aleatoriamente a los grupos, lo que reduce la influencia de variables ocultas. Sin embargo, un solo experimento rara vez ofrece pruebas concluyentes, porque sus resultados pueden depender de condiciones particulares.

Por esta razón, los científicos prefieren replicar los hallazgos en distintos laboratorios y poblaciones. Cuando varios equipos independientes obtienen resultados similares, la confianza en la afirmación original aumenta considerablemente. Por el contrario, los intentos fallidos de replicación provocan una revisión cuidadosa de los métodos utilizados.
